source.title: Squarefree values of polynomial discriminants I
source.authors: Manjul Bhargava, Arul Shankar and Xiaoheng Wang
readSections: The entire arXiv v3 (31 December 2021, dated January 4, 2022; 29 pages; §§1–5 and references), read 2026-09-22. PDF from arxiv.org, SHA-256 6a7252706b283de3f1ee254fe6b56fd76e215f789550346aba12861dfd02af83. The Inventiones version (published online 4 February 2022) is paywalled and was not read; v3 was posted five weeks earlier; identity with the version of record has not been established. Locators are v3 pages.
Part II (arXiv 2207.05592v1) was consulted only to see whether it revisits Part I's arguments; it does not.

Independent review by Codex — codex-a71f92, 2026-09-23: all 29 pages of the same arXiv v3 read; pages 15 and 24–26 checked as rendered pages, and §§2–4 formulas checked in extracted text. Wang's author-hosted 2013 thesis §§1.2.2 and 2.6–2.7, Summary 2.32 and Theorem 2.33 checked; Dietmann arXiv:1010.5341v1 read in full; Shankar–Tsimerman author preprint dated 4 October 2013 read in full. The version of record was not accessible as full text: no finding here claims comparison with the published text.

summary: The paper states positive densities for squarefree discriminants and maximal monogenic orders, with power-saving errors, and lower bounds for monogenic S_n-fields and fields with short integral generators. The independent review requires revision: the arXiv-v3 proof needs nonzero-discriminant restrictions, the root-expanding scaling must be rho^n f(x/rho), the trace-zero squarefree density is zero for n=2, and the asserted density-one uniqueness of Minkowski-reduced bases is false even up to independent signs. Even-degree distinguished flags require B(Y',Y)=0 and a fixed ruling. These failures concern auxiliary statements and proof steps; this review does not disprove Theorems 1.1–1.2 or Corollaries 1.3–1.4. Seventeen version-qualified source issues are recorded. Four items are library-supported by explicit pinned declarations and routine compositions; two are planned; 68 are missing and routed once. Broad roadmap ownership is not a proof of the source-specific statements, and the extraction remains partial pending the closure and API work detailed in the review report.

items.name: Monic polynomials ordered by height
items.statement: V_n(Z) is the set of monic integer polynomials f(x) = x^n + a_1x^{n−1} + ⋯ + a_n of degree n (and V_n(R), V_n(Z_p) the real and p-adic analogues). The height is H(f) = max{|a_1|, |a_2|^{1/2}, …, |a_n|^{1/n}}, and #{f ∈ V_n(Z) : H(f) < X} = 2^nX^{n(n+1)/2} + O(X^{n(n+1)/2−1}). For S ⊂ V_n(Z), S_X is the set of elements of S of height < X. Volumes on V_n(Z_p) (resp. V_n(R)) are normalised so that V_n(Z_p) has volume 1 (resp. V_n(Z) has covolume 1).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The discriminant of a polynomial
items.statement: For a monic polynomial f of positive degree, Δ(f) is its polynomial discriminant; Res(f,f′)=(-1)^{n(n-1)/2}Δ(f). For the universal monic degree-n polynomial this is an integer polynomial in its coefficients.
items.locator: §1, p.1; proof of Proposition 2.2, p.9, arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Resultant/Basic.lean:930 at 082e2d3 (the Sylvester-matrix definition, with the sign that makes real-rooted polynomials have non-negative discriminant).

items.name: Yamamura's density λ_n(p) of p² ∤ Δ
items.statement: For p ≠ 2 let λ_1(p) = 1, λ_2(p) = 1 − 1/p², and λ_n(p) = 1 − (3p^{n−1} − p^{n−2} + (−1)^n(p − 1)²)/(p^n(p + 1)) for n ≥ 3; let λ_1(2) = 1 and λ_n(2) = 1/2 for n ≥ 2. Then λ_n(p) is the density of monic f ∈ V_n(Z_p) with p² ∤ Δ(f) (Yamamura [26, Proposition 3]).
items.note: Checked by exhaustive count modulo p² for n ≤ 5 and p ∈ {2, 3, 5} whenever p^{2n} ≤ 2·10⁶ (for example λ_4(5) = 564/625). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The constants λ_n and their limit λ
items.statement: λ_n := ∏_p λ_n(p) > 0, and λ_n → λ = (1/2)·∏_{p≥3}(1 − (3p − 1)/(p²(p + 1))) ≈ 30.7056% as n → ∞ (2). So as the degree grows, the probability that a random monic integer polynomial has squarefree discriminant tends to λ.
items.note: Computed with PARI: λ = 0.3070556828588…; λ_3, …, λ_8 ≈ 0.3426, 0.2997, 0.3091, 0.3064, 0.3072, 0.3070. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Lenstra's density ρ_n(p) = 1 − 1/p² of p-maximality
items.statement: For n > 1 and every prime p, the density of monic f ∈ V_n(Z_p) such that Z_p[x]/(f(x)) is the maximal order of Q_p[x]/(f(x)) is ρ_n(p) = 1 − 1/p², independently of n (H. W. Lenstra; [1, Proposition 3.5]). Hence ∏_pρ_n(p) = ζ(2)^{−1} ≈ 60.7927%.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: A squarefree discriminant forces maximality
items.statement: If the discriminant of an order Z[θ] in a number field is squarefree, the order is maximal: Δ(minpoly θ) = [O_K : Z[θ]]²·disc(K). Hence the irreducible polynomials counted in Theorem 1.1 are among those counted in Theorem 1.2.
items.note: Library-supported routine composition, not a declaration already named for this corollary: for an integral primitive element θ, the index formula at TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Index/Discriminant.lean:56 makes index(θ)^2 divide the minimal-polynomial discriminant. Squarefree (Mathlib/Algebra/Squarefree/Basic.lean:42) makes this integer index a unit; positivity at Index/Basic.lean:147 makes it 1; index_eq_one_iff at line 154 gives Z[θ]=O_K. All types read at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174 and TauCeti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369. This does not cite not_dvd_index_of_not_dvd_discr_minpoly as if p∤Δ followed from squarefreeness.

items.name: Squarefree discriminant implies Galois group S_n
items.statement: If f is a monic irreducible integer polynomial of degree n with squarefree discriminant, then the Galois group of its splitting field is S_n (see [20], [25], [16], [15]). Equivalently, a degree-n number field with squarefree discriminant has associated Galois group S_n.
items.note: Proof idea: the inertia groups are generated by transpositions and generate a normal transitive subgroup. Not in the atlas: PolynomialGaloisGroups Layer 3 treats the discriminant and A_n only. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Monogenic number fields
items.statement: A number field K is monogenic if there exists θ ∈ O_K with Algebra.adjoin Z {θ}=O_K.
items.note: Tau Ceti also has isMonogenic_iff_exists_index_eq_one (same file).

items.name: The absolute discriminant of a number field
items.statement: The absolute (over Q) discriminant discr(K) is the signed integer discriminant of O_K. Corollary 1.3 orders fields by |discr(K)|; Corollary 1.4 instead orders them by the size of a shortest integral field generator.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Defs.lean:36 at 082e2d3.

items.name: Hilbert irreducibility for monic polynomials by height
items.statement: A density of 100% of monic integer polynomials of degree n, ordered by H, are irreducible over Q and have Galois group S_n (Hilbert's irreducibility theorem). Consequently it does not matter whether irreducibility is imposed in Theorems 1.1–1.2.
items.note: IG.2 supplies qualitative Hilbert irreducibility, not a density-one theorem for this weighted box. Route this quantitative consequence with item 53: outside O(X^{D-n+1}) polynomials, the generic one-parameter group is S_n; Dietmann's resolvent count with T=X^n bounds all proper-group specializations by O_epsilon(X^{D-n/2+epsilon}), with D=n(n+1)/2 and n>=2. The exceptional count for n=1 is trivial. Proposition 4.3 alone only removes reducible/quadratic-factorization polynomials and does not prove that every other Galois group is S_n.

items.name: Strong and weak divisibility of the discriminant by p²
items.statement: For a prime p and monic f ∈ V_n(Z) with p² | Δ(f), p² strongly divides Δ(f) if p² | Δ(f + pg) for every integer polynomial g of degree less than n (the paper says "of degree n"; since the leading coefficient of f + pg is then a p-adic unit, the two readings agree); otherwise p² weakly divides Δ(f).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Root-theoretic criterion for strong and weak divisibility (p odd)
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime and p² | Δ(f). Then p² strongly divides Δ(f) if and only if f mod p has at least two distinct multiple roots in F̄_p or a root in F_p of multiplicity ≥ 3; p² weakly divides Δ(f) if and only if f mod p has exactly one multiple root in F̄_p and it is a double root in F_p. For p = 2 every divisibility 4 | Δ(f) is strong (Stickelberger: Δ(f) ≡ 0 or 1 mod 4 for every lift), so W^{(2)}_m = ∅ for even m. The implication "two multiple roots or a triple root ⇒ strong" holds for every p, and it is the one used in Proposition 2.2.
items.locator: §1, p.4, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (error E1: stated for all p)
items.note: Checked by brute force over all f mod p for n ≤ 5, p ∈ {3, 5} (no exceptions), and p = 2, n = 2, …, 5 (failures, e.g. x² + 1 ≡ (x + 1)²). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Collections of local specifications and κ-acceptability
items.statement: A collection of local specifications is Σ = (Σ_v)_v with Σ_p ⊂ V_n(Z_p) defined by congruence conditions modulo some power of p, and Σ_∞ ⊂ V_n(R) the degree-n polynomials whose number of real roots lies in a fixed nonempty subset of {0, …, n}. V(Σ) is the set of f ∈ V_n(Z) with f ∈ Σ_v for all v. Σ is κ-acceptable if every Σ_p is defined modulo p^κ and, for all sufficiently large p, Σ_p contains every f ∈ V_n(Z_p) with p² ∤ Δ(f). The specifications of Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 are 2-acceptable.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 2.2 (the shape of a weakly divisible polynomial)
items.statement: Let m be a positive squarefree integer and f a monic integer polynomial whose discriminant is weakly divisible by p² for all p | m. Then there is an integer ℓ with f(x + ℓ) = x^n + b_1x^{n−1} + ⋯ + b_{n−1}x + b_n, m | b_{n−1} and m² | b_n (9). The proof reduces to m = p by CRT, moves the double root to 0, and uses the identity Δ(f) = b_nΔ_1 + b_{n−1}²Δ_3 with Δ_1 ∈ Z[b_1, …, b_n], Δ_3 ∈ Z[b_1, …, b_{n−1}] (10), obtained from the Sylvester matrix of Res(f, f′). The integer ℓ is unique mod m.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2 and proof, pp.8–9; remark after Theorem 2.3, p.10, arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The representation of SO_n on symmetric matrices
items.statement: A_0 is the n × n symmetric matrix with 1s on the anti-diagonal. G = SO(A_0) (n = 2g + 1) or G = SO(A_0)/μ_2 = PSO_n (n = 2g + 2) acts on the space W of symmetric n × n matrices by γ·B = γBγ^t. The invariant polynomial of B is f_B(x) = (−1)^{n(n−1)/2}det(A_0x − B), a monic polynomial of degree n (the sign is (−1)^g for n odd and (−1)^{g+1} for n even). Δ(B) := Δ(f_B) and H(B) := H(f_B). (1/2)W(Z) and (1/4)W(Z) are the lattices of B with coefficient denominators dividing 2 and 4.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The invariant ring of W
items.statement: The ring of polynomial invariants for the action of G(C) on W(C) is freely generated by the coefficients of the invariant polynomial f_B(x) ([3, §4]; for n even, [23, §2.1–2.2]).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Stabilizers are the 2-torsion of the Jacobian
items.statement: Let k have characteristic ≠ 2 and f ∈ k[x] monic of degree n with Δ(f) ≠ 0; C_f : y² = f(x) is the smooth hyperelliptic curve of genus g, with one rational Weierstrass point at infinity (n odd) or two rational non-Weierstrass points at infinity (n even), and J_f is its Jacobian. The stabilizer in G(k) of any B ∈ W(k) with f_B = f is naturally isomorphic to J_f[2](k), so has order ≤ #J_f[2](k̄) = 2^{2g} ([4, Proposition 5.1] for n odd; [24, Proposition 2.33] for n even).
items.locator: §2.1, p.7; §3.1, p.15, citing [4], [24], arXiv:1611.09806v3; even-case supplier corrected to Wang, Thesis, Proposition 1.29 and Corollary 1.33, pp.29–30 (not its Theorem 2.33)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Distinguished elements and orbits
items.statement: Let char(k)≠2, g>=1 and Δ(B)≠0. For n=2g+1, B is k-distinguished if a g-dimensional k-subspace is isotropic for both A_0 and B. For n=2g+2, fix the ruling of A_0-maximal isotropic (g+1)-planes containing the standard Y_0=span(e_1,...,e_{g+1}); B is distinguished if there is a k-flag X⊂Y with dim X=g, dim Y=g+1, A_0|Y=0, Y in that ruling, and B(X,Y)=0. Equivalently, for T=A_0^{-1}B, Y=X+TX is maximal A_0-isotropic in the fixed ruling. The rational distinguished orbit is the trivial J_f[2]-torsor class. W^dist denotes the Q-distinguished locus.
items.note: The printed even-degree criterion only says B|X=0; this defines too many flags. The bilinear orthogonality and ruling conditions are essential. The required flag/torsor API still needs decomposition; no completed source route is asserted.

items.name: Isotropic subspaces of a distinguished element
items.statement: For char(k)≠2, g>=1, Δ(f_B)≠0 and B k-distinguished, the set of simultaneous isotropic g-planes (odd n), or the corrected fixed-ruling flags of item 18 (even n), is a trivial J_f[2]-torsor. After choosing one k-point it is in bijection with J_f[2](k), and has at most 2^{2g} elements. The even-degree assertion does not hold for the larger flag set printed in §3.1.
items.locator: §2.1, p.7; §3.1, p.15, citing [4], [24], arXiv:1611.09806v3; even-case supplier Wang Thesis Corollary 1.33 and §2.7; E17
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: J_f[2](k) and factorizations of f
items.statement: For n odd, J_f[2](k) is in natural bijection with the even-degree factors of f over k ([4, Proposition 5.1]); for n even, with the even-degree factorizations of f over k ([5, Proposition 22]). Over k̄ there are 2^{2g} of them. In particular J_f[2](k) is trivial if f is irreducible over k and, for n even, does not factor as g(x)ḡ(x) over a quadratic extension of k.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The subspace W_0 and its parabolic G_0
items.statement: For n = 2g + 1, W_0 ⊂ W is the subspace of B whose top left g × g block is 0, and G_0 ⊂ G is the subgroup of γ such that γ^t preserves the span Y_g of the first g basis vectors; γ ∈ G_0 has block form (γ_1 0; δ γ_2) (5) and acts on the top right g × (g + 1) block by (γ·B)^top = γ_1B^topγ_2^t. For n = 2g + 2, W_0 is the subspace of B whose top left g × (g + 1) block is 0, and G_0 is the parabolic subgroup of γ with γ^t preserving the flag Y_g ⊂ Y_{g+1}; γ has the block form (24) with blocks γ_1, α, γ_2 and again (γ·B)^top = γ_1B^topγ_2^t. Elements of W_0(k) with nonzero discriminant are k-distinguished.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The Q-invariant of 2 ⊗ g ⊗ (g + 1)
items.statement: Write v ∈ V_g = 2 ⊗ g ⊗ (g + 1) as a pair (A, B) of g × (g + 1) matrices, a representation of H_g = SL_2 × GL_g × GL_{g+1}. Let M_v(x, y) be the vector whose i-th coordinate is (−1)^{i−1} times the g × g minor of Ax − By omitting the i-th column; these are g + 1 binary forms of degree g. Q(v) is the determinant of the (g + 1) × (g + 1) matrix of their coefficients. It is a relative invariant: Q((γ_0, γ_1, γ_2)·v) = det(γ_1)^{g+1}det(γ_2)^gQ(v) (6), invariant under SL_2 × SL_g × SL_{g+1}. By SL_2-invariance it is homogeneous of degree g(g + 1)/2 in B.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The Q-invariant on W_0
items.statement: For B ∈ W_0 put Q(B) := Q(A_0^top, B^top), using the top right g × (g + 1) blocks ((7), (25)). It is a relative invariant of G_0: Q(γ·B) = det(γ_1)Q(B) for n odd (8), and Q(γ·B) = det(γ_1)^{g+1}det(γ_2)^gQ(B) = det(γ_1)α^{−g}Q(B) for n even (26).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Q² divides the discriminant on W_0
items.statement: As polynomials in the coordinates of W_0, the discriminant Δ is divisible by Q². So Δ restricted to W_0 is not squarefree and the Ekedahl sieve does not apply to it; moreover σ_m(f), viewed in (1/2)W_0(Z), has discriminant strongly divisible by p² for every p | m, even though Δ(f) is only weakly divisible.
items.locator: §1, p.5; remark after Theorem 2.3, p.10, arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: Asserted "as we will show in the sequel" but not proved in the paper. Q² | Δ was checked at 53–60 random points of W_0(Z) for each n = 3, …, 7. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 2.1 (|Q| is well defined, n odd)
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 1 and B ∈ W_0(Q) with f_B irreducible over Q. Then Q(B′) = ±Q(B) for every B′ ∈ W_0(Q) that is G(Z)-equivalent to B. Proof: Y_g and γ^tY_g are both isotropic for A_0 and B, and J_f[2](Q) is trivial, so γ ∈ G_0(Z), and (8) applies.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 3.1 (|Q| is well defined, n even)
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 2 and B ∈ W_0(Q) with f_B irreducible over Q and, when n ≥ 4, not of the form g(x)ḡ(x) over a quadratic extension of Q. Then Q(B′) = ±Q(B) for every B′ ∈ W_0(Q) that is G(Z)-equivalent to B.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source. Uses the corrected fixed-ruling, B(X,Y)=0 flag torsor of items 18–19, not the printed flag predicate (E17).

items.name: The |Q|-invariant and the sets L
items.statement: For B ∈ W(Q) that is G(Z)-equivalent to some B′ ∈ W_0(Q), with f_B irreducible (and, for n even, not g(x)ḡ(x) over a quadratic field), |Q|(B) := |Q(B′)|, independent of B′ by Propositions 2.1 and 3.1. L is the set of v ∈ (1/2)W(Z) (n odd), resp. v ∈ (1/4)W(Z) (n even), that are G(Z)-equivalent to an element of (1/2)W_0(Z), resp. (1/4)W_0(Z), with f_v satisfying these conditions; L ⊂ W^dist. N(L; M; X) is the number of G(Z)-classes in L with |Q| > M and height < X.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The matrices B_m(c_1, …, c_n) for odd n (11)
items.statement: For n = 2g + 1 with g>=1 and integers m, c_1, …, c_n, B_m ∈ (1/2)W_0(Z) is the symmetric matrix with b_{1,n−1} = b_{n−1,1} = m, b_{i,n−i} = 1 for 2 ≤ i ≤ n − 2, whose lower right (g + 1) × (g + 1) block (rows and columns g + 1, …, n) is tridiagonal with diagonal −c_1, −c_3, …, −c_n and off-diagonal entries −c_2/2, −c_4/2, …, −c_{n−1}/2, and whose other entries are 0. Then f_{B_m}(x) = x^n + c_1x^{n−1} + ⋯ + c_{n−2}x² + mc_{n−1}x + m²c_n and Q(B_m) = ±m, and for every integer ℓ, f_{B+ℓA_0}(x) = f_B(x − ℓ) (12) and Q(B + ℓA_0) = Q(B) (13).
items.note: Verified symbolically for g = 1, 2, 3. With the minor-sign convention of p.7, Q(B_m) = m for g = 1, 3 and −m for g = 2 (the ordering of the coefficient matrix is not fixed; only |Q| is used). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 2.3 (the embedding σ_m, n odd)
items.statement: Let n=2g+1 with g>=1 be odd and m a positive squarefree integer. There is a map σ_m : W^{(2)}_m → (1/2)W_0(Z) with f_{σ_m(f)} = f and Q(σ_m(f)) = m (14), namely σ_m(f) = B_m(c_1, …, c_n) + ℓA_0 where f(x + ℓ) = x^n + c_1x^{n−1} + ⋯ + mc_{n−1}x + m²c_n (Proposition 2.2). No two elements of the image are G(C)-equivalent.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 2.4 (orbits of |Q|-invariant m, n odd)
items.statement: Let W^{(2),irr}_m be the irreducible polynomials in W^{(2)}_m. There is an injective map σ̄_m : W^{(2),irr}_m → G(Z)\L with f_{σ̄_m(f)} = f, and every B in an orbit in the image has |Q|(B) = m. Hence the left side of Theorem 1.5(b), up to reducible polynomials, is at most N(L; M; X).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The matrices B_m(c_1, …, c_n) for even n (27)
items.statement: For n = 2g + 2 with g>=1 and integers m, c_1, …, c_n, B_m ∈ (1/4)W_0(Z) is the symmetric matrix with b_{1,n−1} = b_{n−1,1} = m, b_{i,n−i} = 1 for 2 ≤ i ≤ n − 2, b_{g+1,g+2} = b_{g+2,g+1} = −c_1/2, whose lower right (g + 1) × (g + 1) block (rows and columns g + 2, …, n) is tridiagonal with diagonal c_1²/4 − c_2, −c_4, −c_6, …, −c_n and off-diagonal entries −c_3/2, −c_5/2, …, −c_{n−1}/2, and whose other entries are 0. Then f_{B_m}(x) = x^n + c_1x^{n−1} + ⋯ + c_{n−2}x² + mc_{n−1}x + m²c_n and Q(B_m) = ±m.
items.note: Verified symbolically for g = 1, 2, 3 (Q = m for g = 1, 3, −m for g = 2). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 3.2 (the embedding σ_m, n even)
items.statement: Let n=2g+2 with g>=1 be even and m a positive squarefree integer. There is a map σ_m : W^{(2)}_m → (1/4)W(Z), with image in (1/4)W_0(Z), such that f_{σ_m(f)} = f and Q(σ_m(f)) = m (28), namely σ_m(f) = B_m(c_1, …, c_n) + ℓA_0.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 3.3 (orbits of |Q|-invariant m, n even)
items.statement: Let W^{(2),irr}_m be the polynomials in W^{(2)}_m that are irreducible over Q and do not factor as g(x)ḡ(x) over any quadratic extension of Q. There is an injective map σ̄_m : W^{(2),irr}_m → G(Z)\L with f_{σ̄_m(f)} = f for every f ∈ W^{(2),irr}_m, and every element of every orbit in the image has |Q|-invariant m.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The tail sets W^{(1)}_m, W^{(2)}_m and W_m
items.statement: For squarefree m > 0, W^{(1)}_m (resp. W^{(2)}_m) is the set of f ∈ V_n(Z) whose discriminant is strongly (resp. weakly) divisible by p² for every prime p | m; W_m is the set of f ∈ V_n(Z) with m² | Δ(f); a subscript X restricts to height < X. The summed tail statements 55–56 use W_m^nz={f∈W_m:Δ(f)≠0}; W_m itself is retained for the original union estimates. The distinction is mandatory (E13).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Iwasawa decomposition and a Siegel-set fundamental set
items.statement: G(R) = N(R)TK with N the lower-triangular unipotent group, T the split torus and K compact, and a fundamental set F for the left action of G(Z) on G(R) can be taken inside a Siegel set N′T′K, with N′ absolutely bounded and T′ = {(s) : s_i ≥ c}.
items.note: AA.3 plans Siegel sets, their height estimates and the finite covering of arithmetic quotients. The source-specific single-Siegel-set assertion and the Iwasawa coordinate normalization still need their exact supplier proofs; the general finite-cover statement is not a substitute for checking this application.

items.name: Reduction to an integral over the torus (odd n)
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 1, R a bounded fundamental domain for G(R) on {B ∈ W(R) : Δ(B) ≠ 0, H(B) < 1} ([4, §9.1]), and G_1 ⊂ G(R) a compact left K-invariant set that is the closure of a nonempty open set. Since (Fh)·(XR) covers a fundamental domain at most 2^{2g} times, N(L; M; X) ≪ #{B ∈ (Fh)·(XR) ∩ L : |Q|(B) > M} (15); averaging over h ∈ G_1 gives (16), and with the Haar measure dγ = dn δ(s)d^×s dk, δ(s) = ∏_{k=1}^g s_k^{k²−2kg} (17), s_i = t_i/t_{i+1} (i < g), s_g = t_g, and the bounded set E = N″KG_1R, N(L; M; X) ≪ ∫_{s_i≫1}#{B ∈ ((s)·XE) ∩ L : |Q|(B) > M}δ(s)d^×s (18).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Reduction to an integral over the torus (even n)
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 2, with R and F as in [23, §4.1], s_i = t_i/t_{i+1} for 1 ≤ i ≤ g and s_{g+1} = t_gt_{g+1}, d^×s = ∏_{i=1}^{g+1}ds_i/s_i, and δ(s) = ∏_{k=1}^{g−1}s_k^{k²−2kg−k}·(s_gs_{g+1})^{−g(g+1)/2} (30). Then N(L; M; X) ≪ ∫_{γ∈F}#{B ∈ ((γG_1)·(XR)) ∩ L : |Q|(B) > M}dγ (29) and N(L; M; X) ≪ ∫_{s_i≫1}#{B ∈ ((s)·XE) ∩ L : |Q|(B) > M}δ(s)d^×s (31), with E = N″KG_1R bounded.
items.note: δ(s) is the modular character of the D_{g+1} root system in these coordinates, checked against 2ρ. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Torus weights of the coordinates and of Q (even n)
items.statement: For n = 2g + 2 and T = diag(t_1^{−1}, …, t_{g+1}^{−1}, t_{g+1}, …, t_1), the weight of b_ij is t_i^{−1}t_j^{−1} (i, j ≤ g + 1), t_i^{−1}t_{n−j+1} (i ≤ g + 1 < j), t_{n−i+1}t_{n−j+1} (i, j > g + 1) (32), and w(Q) = (t_1⋯t_g)^{−1}t_{g+1}^g = ∏_{k=1}^gs_k^{−k} (36, corrected). Every entry of B ∈ (s)·XE is ≪ Xw(b_ij), and |Q(B)| ≪ X^{g(g+1)/2}w(Q).
items.note: Checked symbolically for g ≤ 5: with s_{g+1} = t_gt_{g+1}, (t_1⋯t_g)^{−1}t_{g+1}^g = ∏s_k^{−k}, as the proof of Proposition 3.6 uses. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 2.5 (most distinguished points lie in W_00, odd n)
items.statement: Let W_00 ⊂ W be the symmetric matrices with b_ij = 0 whenever i + j < n. Then ∫_{s_i≫1}#{B ∈ ((s)·XE) ∩ ((1/2)W(Z) ∖ (1/2)W_00(Z)) : b_11 = 0}δ(s)d^×s = O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2−1+ε}) (20) and ∫_{s_i≫1}#{B ∈ ((s)·XE) ∩ L : b_11 ≠ 0}δ(s)d^×s = o(X^{n(n+1)/2}) (21) ([4, Propositions 10.5 and 10.7]).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Distinguished elements have p-adic density bounded away from 1
items.statement: The p-adic density of Q_p-distinguished elements of W(Z_p) is bounded uniformly away from 1: for n = 2g + 1 it is at most 1 − g/(2g + 1) + O(1/p) ([4, §10.7]); for n even this is shown in the proof of [23, Proposition 23].
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.6, p.13; proof of Proposition 3.5, p.19, citing [4], [23], arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: The Selberg-sieve step of Shankar–Tsimerman
items.statement: The Shankar–Tsimerman Selberg step requires both local exclusions of density bounded away from 0 and 1 and a uniform congruence-count remainder. For the BSW main-body averaged count, the required input is r_d=O_epsilon(X^{D-1} d^{1+epsilon}) for squarefree d, D=n(n+1)/2. With the optimized Selberg bound, the sifted count is O_epsilon(X^D L^{-1/2+epsilon}+X^{D-1}L^{2+epsilon}); choosing L=X^{2/5} yields O_epsilon(X^{D-1/5+epsilon}). Local densities alone do not imply this saving.
items.locator: Proofs of Propositions 2.6 and 3.5, pp.13, 19, citing [22], arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: The uniform remainder for the orthogonal representation is a separate prerequisite, not established merely by [22]'s quintic example. Shankar–Tsimerman author preprint §§1.1 and 3, pp.2,4–5, was read by the reviewer; it explicitly requires such a uniform estimate. This dependency remains a closure gap.

items.name: Optimized Selberg upper bound, importing the existing Lambda-squared mechanism
items.statement: For a nonnegative finite sieve sequence with ∑_{d|n}a_n=A g(d)+r_d, squarefree sieve support P(z), 0<g(p)<1, h(d)=∏_{p|d}g(p)/(1-g(p)), and G(L)=∑_{d<sqrt(L),d|P(z)}h(d), the optimized Selberg inequality bounds the sifted sum by A/G(L)+∑_{d<L,d|P(z)}τ_3(d)|r_d|. Weight normalization, optimal main-term construction and this coefficient-size bound are part of the contract. The general Lambda-squared upper-bound mechanism is already in Mathlib.
items.locator: Proofs of Propositions 2.6 and 3.5, pp.13, 19, arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: Mathlib at 082e2d3: BoundingSieve.siftedSum_le_mainSum_errSum_of_upperMoebius (NumberTheory/SelbergSieve.lean:216), BoundingSieve.upperMoebius_lambdaSquared (:250), and BoundingSieve.mainSum_lambdaSquared_eq_sum_mul_sum_sq (:375) supply the mechanism and diagonalization. The enclosing namespace is BoundingSieve, not SelbergSieve. SV.1 owns the missing optimization and coefficient bound required by Shankar–Tsimerman §3, equation (6), and RS-07. No duplicate proof of the existing Lambda-squared construction is planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.7 (large |Q| in the cusp, odd n)
items.statement: ∫_{s_i≫1}#{B ∈ ((s)·XE) ∩ L ∩ (1/2)W_00(Z) : |Q|(B) > M}δ(s)d^×s = O(X^{n(n+1)/2}log X/M). items.name: Bhargava's quantitative Ekedahl sieve ([2, Theorem 3.3]) in weighted form
items.statement: Let Y ⊂ A^n_Z be a closed subscheme of codimension k ≥ 2 and B ⊂ R^n a bounded region with a reasonable boundary. Then #{a ∈ rB ∩ Z^n : a mod p ∈ Y(F_p) for some prime p > M} = O(r^n/(M^{k−1}log M) + r^{n−k+1}). The same proof applies to weighted homogeneous expansions and to a union over squarefree m > M of the conditions at all p | m; for the codimension-2 locus of polynomials with two multiple roots or a triple root it gives Theorem 1.5(a), with the smaller second error term O(X^{n(n+1)/2−1}) because a_n has the largest range.
items.note: The adaptation is asserted, not written out. The same external theorem is routed to ST.2 by PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 1.5(a) (tail estimate, strongly divisible case)
items.statement: For every M > 0 and ε > 0, #⋃_{m>M, m squarefree}{f ∈ W^{(1)}_m : H(f) < X} = O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2+ε}/M) + O(X^{n(n+1)/2−1}), with implied constants independent of M and X.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 1.5(b) (tail estimate, weakly divisible case)
items.statement: For every M > 0 and ε > 0, #⋃_{m>M, m squarefree}{f ∈ W^{(2)}_m : H(f) < X} = O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2+ε}/M) + O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2−1/5+ε}), with implied constants independent of M and X. For odd n it follows from Theorem 2.4 and Propositions 2.5–2.7, for even n from Theorem 3.3 and Propositions 3.4–3.6, together with Proposition 4.3.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 4.2 (polynomials with a rational root)
items.statement: The number of f ∈ V_n(Z)_X with a rational linear factor is O(X^{n(n+1)/2−n+1}log X). Proof: a_n = 0 gives O(X^{n(n+1)/2−n}); otherwise count (a_1, …, a_{n−2}, a_n, r) with r | a_n, which determines a_{n−1}, using Σ_{|a_n|≤X^n}d(a_n) ≪ X^nlog X.
items.locator: Lemma 4.2 and proof, p.21, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (gap E8)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Dietmann's quantitative Hilbert irreducibility ([7, Lemma 2, Lemma 4, Theorem 1])
items.statement: For n>=2, fixing a_1,...,a_{n-2}, at most n^2+n values of a_{n-1} make x^n+a_1x^{n-1}+...+a_{n-1}x+t have generic Galois group different from S_n (Dietmann Lemma 2, r=n-1). Thus the weighted |a_i|<=X^i box has O(X^{(n-1)(n-2)/2}) exceptional (n-1)-tuples. For a nonexceptional tuple with |a_i|<=T and T>=1, and a subgroup H<S_n, the uniform resolvent/plane-curve argument bounds specializations |t|<=T with Galois group conjugate to H by O_{n,epsilon}(T^{1/[S_n:H]+epsilon}). The polynomial-coefficient bound is essential for uniformity. An intransitive root-action subgroup without fixed points has index at least binomial(n,2), for n>=4: it preserves an orbit of size k with 2<=k<=n-2. This elementary argument supplies the small-degree cases not covered by the n>=9 hypothesis of Dietmann's Lemma 4.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.3, p.22, citing [7], arXiv:1611.09806v3; Dietmann arXiv:1010.5341v1, Lemmas 2,4–6 and §3, pp.3–5
items.note: Independently read at https://arxiv.org/pdf/1010.5341v1. The paper's Theorem 1 is a uniform coefficient-box result, not a theorem with arbitrarily large fixed coefficients hidden inside an epsilon-only constant. T=X^n satisfies all coefficient bounds needed here. The supplier's resolvent and plane-curve counting inputs still need explicit import nodes in a completed extraction.

items.name: Proposition 4.3 (reducible polynomials are negligible)
items.statement: Let V_n(Z)^red consist of reducible monic degree-n polynomials and, for even n>=4, irreducible polynomials factoring as g(x)gbar(x) over a quadratic extension of Q. For n>=2, n≠4, the argument gives #V_n(Z)^red_X=O(X^{D-n+1}log X), D=n(n+1)/2. For n=4, the verified argument gives O_epsilon(X^{22/3+epsilon}), not the printed O(X^7 log X). The stronger quartic estimate is not an established item of this extraction. Both bounds are smaller than the X^{D-1/5+epsilon} error required by the main sieve.
items.locator: Proposition 4.3 and proof, pp.21–22, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (error E7)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 4.4 (uniformity for m² | Δ)
items.statement: For M>0 and X>=2, with W_m^nz defined in item 34, ∑_{m>M,m squarefree}#W^nz_{m,X}=O_epsilon(X^{D+epsilon}/sqrt(M))+O_epsilon(X^{D-1/5+epsilon}), D=n(n+1)/2. For a nonzero discriminant, the number of squarefree square divisors is O_epsilon(X^epsilon). Splitting its primes into strong and weak parts and using Theorem 1.5 gives the estimate. The unrestricted sum printed in (39) is infinite, since x^n has discriminant zero for n>=2 (E13).
items.locator: Theorem 4.4 and proof, pp.22–23, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (misprint E5)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Remark after Theorem 4.4 (the denominator √M improves to M)
items.statement: The √M in (39) can be improved to M: on the nonzero-discriminant locus only, split W_m into W^{(1)}_{m_1} ∩ W^{(2)}_{m_2} over dyadic ranges of m_1, m_2, embed W^{(2)}_{m_2} into (1/4)W(Z), and in the (1/4)W_00(Z) piece impose strong divisibility by p² for p | m_1 and apply the quantitative Ekedahl sieve, saving 1/m_1. This gives O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2+ε}/M) + O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2−1/5+ε}).
items.note: Outlined only. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source. The nonzero-discriminant restriction of E13 is required. The 1/M strengthening remains an outlined target, not an independently closed proof.

items.name: Theorem 4.1 (the squarefree sieve with κ-acceptable conditions)
items.statement: Let κ>=1 and Σ be κ-acceptable. Then the source's target is #V(Σ)_X=Vol(Σ_{infinity,H<1})∏_p Vol(Σ_p) X^D+O_epsilon(X^{D-min{1/5,1/(2κ)}+epsilon}), D=n(n+1)/2. Use inclusion–exclusion first on Δ(f)≠0, where each f fails only finitely many local conditions; separate Δ=0 before summing. Its contribution is O(X^{D-1}) by the nonzero-polynomial lattice-zero bound. The small-modulus lattice error is O(∑_{m<=X^{1/κ}} thetabar(m)m^κ X^{D-1}), and the large-modulus tail uses item 55 on W^nz. The bound on the zero locus and the uniform lattice-count input must be supplied, not replaced by the divergent unrestricted sum.
items.locator: Theorem 4.1, p.21; proof §4.2, (40)–(41), pp.22–23, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (error E6, misprint E5); nonzero-locus correction E13
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (density of squarefree discriminants)
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1. When monic integer polynomials f of degree n are ordered by H(f), the density of those with squarefree discriminant Δ(f) exists and equals λ_n = ∏_pλ_n(p) > 0.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Power-saving count of squarefree discriminants ((4), first line)
items.statement: For n > 1, #{f ∈ V_n(Z) : H(f) < X, Δ(f) squarefree} = λ_n·2^nX^{n(n+1)/2} + O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2−1/5+ε}). Theorem 4.1 with κ = 2 gives it. Since reducible polynomials are fewer than the error term, irreducibility may be imposed.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 1.2 (density of monogenic maximal orders)
items.statement: Let n > 1. When monic integer polynomials f of degree n are ordered by H(f), the density of those for which Z[x]/(f(x)) is the ring of integers of its fraction field is ∏_p(1 − 1/p²) = ζ(2)^{−1}. Since 100% are irreducible with Galois group S_n, about 60.7927% of monic integer polynomials of degree n are irreducible with Z[x]/(f) maximal.

items.name: Signature and local-condition variants
items.statement: Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 remain true for polynomials with a prescribed number of real roots, and with any finite set of local conditions at finitely many places (with positive, easily computable constants) that do not force the counted set to be empty; certain infinite sets of local conditions are allowed (Theorem 4.1).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: The Ellenberg–Venkatesh upper bound ([9, Remark 3.3])
items.statement: The number of number fields K of degree n with s(K) ≤ Y is ≪ Y^{(n−1)(n+2)/2}, where s(K) = inf{‖x‖ : x ∈ O_K, Q(x) = K} and ‖x‖ is the maximum of the archimedean absolute values of x. A bound on ‖x‖ bounds the coefficients of the minimal polynomial; translating x by an integer removes one coefficient.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: The lattice R_g, quasi-reduced and strongly quasi-reduced polynomials
items.statement: For g ∈ V_n(R) with Δ(g) ≠ 0, with r real and 2s complex roots, R[x]/(g(x)) ≅ R^r × C^s ≅ R^n via the real and complex embeddings (C = R + R√−1). R_g is the lattice spanned by 1, θ, …, θ^{n−1}, θ the image of x; for g ∈ V_n(Z), R_g is the image of Z[x]/(g(x)). g is quasi-reduced if there are monic integer polynomials h_i of degree i (1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1) such that 1, h_1(θ), …, h_{n−1}(θ) is a Minkowski-reduced basis of R_g, and strongly quasi-reduced if moreover Z[x]/(g(x)) has a unique Minkowski-reduced basis where throughout the corrected extraction 'unique' means unique up to independent signs of the individual basis vectors; it does not quotient by adding earlier basis vectors or by all lattice isometries.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source. This sign convention repairs the vacuous literal definition but does not make the density-one claim true; see E16.

items.name: Lemma 5.1 (corrected: strongly quasi-reduced polynomials give distinct rings up to x ↦ −x)
items.statement: Let g, g* be monic integer polynomials of degree n with nonzero discriminant, strongly quasi-reduced, with vanishing x^{n−1}-coefficients. If Z[x]/(g(x)) ≅ Z[x]/(g*(x)) as rings, then g*(x) = g(x) or g*(x) = (−1)^ng(−x). (The printed statement concludes g = g*, which fails for the pair g(x), (−1)^ng(−x); E10.)
items.locator: Lemma 5.1 and proof, p.24, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (error E10)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 5.2 (scaling makes a polynomial quasi-reduced)
items.statement: For a monic real polynomial g of degree n with Δ(g)≠0, define the monic root-expanding polynomial g_rho(x)=rho^n g(x/rho), rho>0. For all sufficiently large rho, g_rho is quasi-reduced. Its power basis corresponds to 1,rho θ,...,rho^{n-1}θ^{n-1}; the Gram matrix is ΛQ_1Λ^T and its successive Gram–Schmidt lengths are rho^{i-1}t_i. The well-separated-basis argument in E12 gives quasi-reduction. Also H(g_rho)=rho H(g). Neither the nonmonic g(rho x) nor its monic normalization rho^{-n}g(rho x) has these properties (E14).
items.locator: Lemma 5.2 and proof, pp.24–25, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (gap E12); scaling correction E14
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Corrected weak replacement for Lemma 5.3: density-one quasi-reduction only
items.statement: A density of 100% of monic integer polynomials of fixed degree n ordered by H is quasi-reduced (not necessarily strongly quasi-reduced). The intended compactness proof uses g_rho(x)=rho^n g(x/rho), a compact Jordan-measurable region away from the discriminant locus, positive continuous Gram–Schmidt lengths bounded uniformly on it, and the well-separated-basis lemma. The original stronger uniqueness-up-to-sign density-one assertion is false already for n=2 (E16); it is not an available prerequisite for counting fields.
items.locator: Lemma 5.3 and proof, p.25, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (gap E12); E14 and E16
items.note: This is the safe weaker replacement target, not a claimed proof of strong quasi-reduction or of its restriction to trace-zero/local-condition slices. Complete the quantitative/source dependency decomposition and a separate bounded-multiplicity argument for the field-counting applications.

items.name: Theorem 5.4 (squarefree discriminants with a_1 = 0 or 0 ≤ a_1 < n)
items.statement: For monic degree-n integer polynomials with a_1=0, the source's trace-zero sieve target is density κ_n=∏_p κ_n(p), with κ_n(p) the normalized local measure of p²∤Δ in that slice. The universal assertion κ_n>0 must be removed: for n=2, Δ(x²+a_2)=-4a_2 and κ_2(2)=κ_2=0. For n=1 the single polynomial x has discriminant 1. Positivity in any other slice requires verification of every local obstruction. The band 0<=a_1<n, with claimed density λ_n, is a different assertion and avoids the quadratic trace-zero obstruction. Its restricted tail estimates and local-measure comparison must be retained as separate proof obligations.
items.locator: Theorem 5.4 and the following paragraph, pp.25–26; §2.3, p.11, arXiv:1611.09806v3; E15
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Corollary 1.3 (monogenic S_n-fields)
items.statement: For n>1, the paper states that the number of isomorphism classes of monogenic degree-n number fields with normal-closure group S_n and |disc|<X is ≫X^{1/2+1/n}. The exponent comes from (2+...+n)/(n(n-1))=1/2+1/n and the bound |Δ(f)|≪H(f)^{n(n-1)}. The extracted proof is not closed: Lemma 5.3's strong uniqueness claim is false and the trace-zero squarefree route is empty for n=2. A source-qualified bounded-multiplicity/positive-subfamily argument (or a separate quadratic case) is required. This review does not claim the corollary itself is false.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Remark 5.5 (signatures and local conditions in Corollary 1.3)
items.statement: Corollary 1.3 holds with prescribed real signature, and with any local conditions at a finite set of primes that do not contradict local monogeneity.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source. The 'identical proof' is not certified: trace-zero restrictions, local conditions and multiplicity require the repairs recorded at items 67–69.

items.name: Corollary 1.4 (the Ellenberg–Venkatesh conjecture on short generating vectors)
items.statement: For n>1, the paper states that the number of degree-n number fields with an integral generator of archimedean size <Y is ≍Y^{(n-1)(n+2)/2}, also after requiring normal-closure group S_n. The elementary upper bound translates a generator to 0<=a_1<n before counting its coefficient bounds. For the lower bound the root estimate H(f)<=Y implies ||θ||≪Y, but field multiplicities cannot be removed by the false strong-density assertion (E16), and the trace-zero squarefree family is empty in degree two (E15). The lower-bound proof remains a revision obligation; the corollary is not disproved here.

items.name: Remark 5.6 (conjectural asymptotic for monogenic fields)
items.statement: Conjecture: a positive proportion of monic integer polynomials of degree n with 0 ≤ a_1 < n and |Δ| < X have height O(X^{1/(n(n−1))}); and the number of monogenic number fields of degree n with absolute discriminant < X is asymptotic to (nC_n/(2ζ(2)))X^{1/2+1/n} (42), where C_n is the (n − 1)-dimensional volume of {f ∈ V_n(R) : a_1 = 0, |Δ(f)| < 1}. For n = 3, C_3 = 2^{1/3}(3 + √3)/45·Γ(1/2)Γ(1/6)/Γ(2/3).
items.note: A conjecture. C_3 was checked by direct integration of the area of {|4a_2³ + 27a_3²| < 1}: 0.96530936 against the printed closed form 0.965309365. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Minkowski-reduced bases and the Siegel-set description
items.statement: A Z-basis b_1,...,b_n of a Euclidean lattice is Minkowski-reduced when each b_i is a shortest vector such that b_1,...,b_i extends to a Z-basis. Sign changes preserve this predicate. Reduction theory places normalized reduced Gram forms inside a suitable Siegel set; this is a containment, not an equivalence between an arbitrary Siegel-set point and a Minkowski-reduced basis. Arbitrary Gram determinants require GL_n^+(R), or determinant normalization before SL_n(R). Generic uniqueness in continuous Gram space does not imply density-one uniqueness for lattices from integer polynomials (E16).
items.locator: §5, footnote 1, p.24; proof of Lemma 5.2, p.25, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (gap E12)
items.note: GN.3 owns the reduced-basis carrier and reduction comparison; AA.3 owns general arithmetic-group Siegel sets. The statistical uniqueness assertion is explicitly excluded. The stronger well-separated-basis lemma still needs its own precise theorem/API and is not silently identified with Siegel containment.

items.name: Fujiwara's root bound (corrected)
items.statement: Every root θ of x^n + a_1x^{n−1} + ⋯ + a_n ∈ C[x] satisfies |θ| ≤ 2·max{|a_1|, |a_2|^{1/2}, …, |a_{n−1}|^{1/(n−1)}, |a_n/2|^{1/n}} (Fujiwara [10]). In particular H(f) ≤ Y implies ‖θ‖ ≪ Y.
items.note: Routed to ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.3 as a source. Independently verified by the geometric-series argument: if M is the displayed maximum and |z|>2M, divide f(z)=0 by z^n to get 1<=sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(M/|z|)^i+2(M/|z|)^n<1. M=0 is trivial. routes.reason: ST.0 owns families, heights, local conditions and densities. That covers the family V_n(Z) ordered by the weighted height, Yamamura's density λ_n(p) of p² ∤ Δ, Lenstra's density 1 − 1/p² of p-maximality, the strong/weak dichotomy for p² | Δ with its root criterion and Proposition 2.2, and κ-acceptable local specifications. ST.1 owns integral invariant theory and orbit parametrizations. That covers the representation of SO_n on symmetric matrices with its invariant polynomial, stabilizers J_f[2], distinguished orbits, the subspace W_0 and parabolic G_0, the new Q-invariant of 2 ⊗ g ⊗ (g + 1) with its relative invariance, and the explicit matrices B_m. These give the embeddings σ_m of weakly divisible polynomials (Theorems 2.3–2.4 and 3.2–3.3), which turn weak divisibility into orbits of |Q|-invariant m. The atlas and libraries have the discriminant only; none of these statements appears. Revision gate: use the corrected flag predicate of E17 and provide the hyperelliptic/Jacobian and invariant-theory supplier interfaces; broad ST.1 ownership alone does not close these dependencies.

ST.2 owns counting lattice points in fundamental domains, bounding cusp and reducible contributions, and the uniform tail estimates needed to impose infinitely many local conditions. Its acceptance condition requires exactly this: an interchange of sieve and height limits must come from a uniform tail theorem. The paper is a model case. Its tail estimate (Theorem 1.5) has two parts:
- the strongly divisible part, from the quantitative Ekedahl sieve;
- the weakly divisible part, from counting points of large |Q|-invariant deep in the cusp (Propositions 2.5–2.7 and 3.4–3.6), with the torus-weight bookkeeping and a Selberg-sieve saving off W_00.
It then bounds reducible polynomials (Lemma 4.2, Proposition 4.3) and runs the squarefree sieve with κ-acceptable conditions (Theorems 4.1 and 4.4). None of these statements is in the atlas or the libraries. Revision gate: items 55–57 exclude Δ=0 before summing, item 54 uses the weaker verified quartic bound, and item 42 retains the uniform congruence-error hypothesis. Import the generic Davenport/semialgebraic lattice estimate from GN.4 under RS-07 rather than rebuilding it.

GN.3 owns the definition and reduction theory of Euclidean lattice bases in item 73, importing general Siegel sets from AA.3. This route is restricted to those objects and the one-way reduction-domain comparison. It does not assert generic uniqueness for the integer polynomial family, nor a completed proof of the well-separated-basis lemma.

IG.2 owns the qualitative Hilbert irreducibility foundation; items 10 and 53 provide the source-specific quantitative extension. The weighted density-one conclusion is missing rather than already planned by the qualitative layer. Dietmann's coefficient-controlled resolvent specialization estimate and the exceptional generic-family count yield it. The plane-curve counting theorem and resolvent construction still require explicit supplier imports before this becomes a closed blueprint.

CA.3 owns polynomial arithmetic: resultants, discriminants and irreducibility. Fujiwara's bound on the roots of a monic polynomial in terms of its coefficients is a classical polynomial estimate. It converts the height bound into ‖θ‖ ≪ Y in Corollary 1.4.

sourceIssues.printed: "Then p² strongly divides ∆(f) if and only if f modulo p has at least two distinct multiple roots in F̄_p, or has a root in F_p of multiplicity at least 3; and p² weakly divides ∆(f) if p² | ∆(f) but f modulo p has only one multiple root in F_p and this root is a simple double root."
sourceIssues.correction: This holds for odd p. For p = 2, 4 always divides Δ(f) strongly when 2 | Δ(f), so W^{(2)}_m is empty for even m.
sourceIssues.reason: By Stickelberger's congruence, the discriminant of a monic integer polynomial is ≡ 0 or 1 mod 4, so 2 | Δ(f + 2g) implies 4 | Δ(f + 2g) for every g. For example f = x² + 1 ≡ (x + 1)² mod 2 has a single simple double root, yet Δ(x² + a_1x + a_2) = a_1² − 4a_2 ≡ 0 mod 4 whenever a_1 is even. A brute-force check over all f mod p confirms the criterion for p = 3 (n ≤ 5) and p = 5 (n ≤ 4), and finds failures at p = 2 for every n = 2, …, 5. The proofs only use the implication "two multiple roots or a triple root ⇒ strong", which holds at p = 2 as well (in Proposition 2.2), and the tail estimates concern large primes, so nothing else changes.

It holds for ten distinct flags: (t,r)=(2,0),(3,4),(3,9),(4,2),(4,11),(9,2),(9,11),(10,4),(10,9),(11,0), exceeding #J_f[2](F_13)<=4. All Y_t are in the same ruling as Y_0 (for t≠0 their intersection has even codimension two). For example (t,r)=(3,4) fails B(Y′,Y)=0. The stronger orthogonality is present in the block condition defining W_0 and in Wang's actual torsor description.
